newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN hopes 20,000 Cambodians may stay in Thailand.
newsitem.headline: UN hopes 20,000 Cambodians may stay in Thailand.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said on Tuesday it hoped more than 20,000 Cambodian civilians who fled into Thailand overnight to escape fighting would be allowed to stay until the danger of returning home receded.
Pamela O'Toole, spokeswoman of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, also said UNHCR would distribute 10-day rations of rice and fish to the refugees on Wednesday.
More than 20,000 Cambodian civilians poured across the border to escape fighting in the besieged town of O'Smach between royalist troops holding the town and troops under Cambodian strongman Hun Sen.
Forces loyal to ousted Cambodian premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh have been fighting government troops under Hun Sen since shortly after the prince was ousted on July 6.

"Obviously we would urge the refugees be allowed to stay as long as they may be in danger if they have to return," O'Toole told a news briefing. "I think it (the Thai government) hopes these people would return as and when the fighting subsides.
"Our team on the border says the refugees appear to be in relatively good shape, apart from a number of malaria cases and that their transfer across the border and into the camp was orderly."

Some 40 tonnes of rice and 50,000 tins of fish are to be distributed to the refugees, whom Thai authorities have moved to a camp at Houi Cheund, some seven km (four miles) from the border, according to UNHCR.
"We are also ready to help provide any other items the Thai authorities might need to cope with the influx," O'Toole said.
From the Thai side of the border, UNHCR saw some 25-30 families who had decided to stay on the Cambodian side for the time being, according to the spokeswoman.
